query: Consider the following context: Melting properties are critical for designing novel materials, especially for discovering high-performance, high-melting refractory materials. Experimental measurements of these properties are extremely challenging due to their high melting temperatures. Complementary theoretical predictions are, therefore, indispensable. One of the most accurate approaches for this purpose is the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT). However, it generally involves expensive thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamic simulations. The high computational cost makes high-throughput calculations infeasible. In that context, which method can be used for calculate its melting properties, including the melting temperature, entropy and enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A new computational method based on machine learning potentials can accurately calculate the melting properties of novel refractory materials, including melting temperature, entropy and enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point, with a significantly reduced computational cost compared to the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT).

generation.predicted_outcome: Melting temperature within 10% of experimental values, entropy and enthalpy of fusion within 5% of experimental values, and volume change at the melting point within 2% of experimental values
generation.baseline: Ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT)
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of machine learning potentials for novel refractory materials, potential need for large training datasets

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine learning potentials predict melting properties with an error greater than 20% compared to the ab initio free-energy approach based on density functional theory (DFT) for more than 50% of the tested materials, the hypothesis is falsified
